findings.finding: The table shows no fair value ('אין עדיין שווי אמין להצגה') and scenarios_he.md shows no prices. The cause is the unresolved forecast material issue possible_lender: liabilities are 51,409 of 58,149 total assets (88.4%) at 2026-09-30, with no cost-of-revenue line. The 10-Q balance sheet (pf_10q_20261029, reading/10q_2026-10-29.txt lines 262-318 and Note 8 lines 789-800) resolves the issue in favour of the operating classification, but not for the reason assumed. (1) Client funds are small: settlement obligations 2,151 plus restricted security deposits held for customers 2,231 make 4,382, which is 8.5% of liabilities. Matching assets: settlement assets 1,593, restricted deposits 2,231 and restricted cash 564. (2) Most of the liabilities are ordinary corporate items. Debt is 23,938 (short-term 1,749 plus long-term 22,189), 46.6% of liabilities: bonds that fund buybacks, not deposits. Accrued expenses are 13,950, of which customer incentives are 10,333. Other liabilities are 4,683 and accounts payable 1,083. (3) The ratio is high because buybacks shrank equity: treasury stock is 95,201 against retained earnings of 95,640, leaving total equity of 6,740. (4) There is no loan book: assets hold no loans or receivables from cardholders. Investments are 317. Settlement exposure is guaranteed but 'short-term and generally limited to a few days' (line 1069). Revenue is fees (net revenue 9,807 in Q3), interest expense is 653 for 9M, and the casefile card itself notes capex at 1.5% of revenue. MA is an operating fee platform, and FCFF with debt deducted is the right route; residual income is not.
findings.where: companies/MA/inputs.json forecast.reviews (no 'classification' entry); casefile fc.spec.underwriting.material_issues[0] possible_lender (unresolved), dc.verdict.withheld_reasons[1], out/table_he.md fair-value row, out/scenarios_he.md

findings.finding: The ROICs that set every scenario value through economics (bear 0.30, base 0.50, bull 0.70) are analyst estimates, not measured figures. The engine anchor is fc.anchors.roic 0.94, so these are deliberately lower, and the decimals are correctly typed. They rest on one 9M-2026 reinvestment calculation: net prepaid incentives 4,688 minus amortization 2,030 is about 2.7bn (10-Q lines 431 and 441, verified), plus BVNK at 1.4bn, against NOPAT growth. The pre-2026 prepaid-incentive series was not saved (path.json gaps). The base value of 726 against the bear value of 461 is mostly this choice of ROIC.
findings.fix: Say next to the result that the scenario ROICs are estimates from a single 9M period and that the base value depends on them. If repaired, add the FY2023-FY2025 'prepaid expenses' and 'amortization of customer incentives' lines from the saved 10-K cash flow statement to measure the reinvestment rate over several years.

findings.finding: The multiples sit above a comparable own-history range. Base year 0 is 33.7x forward EPS and bull year 0 is 40.2x. own_history (27.5 / 35.6 / 43.5) is a TRAILING GAAP P/E. path.json itself says a forward range would sit about one year's EPS growth lower, putting the median near 31-32x. So the base starts above the forward-equivalent median and the bull starts near the trailing peak. The multiples converge to 28.9x (base) and 30.6x (bull) by year 5. No named competitor's forward P/E is evidenced.
